scenes.tts: Turn a newt's eye upside down, then cut the optic nerve and let it regrow. Hold a lure above its head, and the newt turns its head down. It kept making that mistake for as long as anyone watched. Each regrown axon went back to the place it came from. How does an axon know where to go?
scenes.visual: Eye flips, nerve cut and regrown with crossed lines, lure and wrong head turn, question marks on target
scenes.narration: Turn a newt's eye upside down, then cut the optic nerve and let it regrow. Hold a lure above its head, and the newt turns its head down. It kept making that mistake for as long as anyone watched. Each regrown axon went back to the place it came from. How does an axon know where to go?

scenes.tts: The retina sends its axons to a target in the midbrain, the tectum. The map is orderly. Neighbors in the retina connect to neighbors in the tectum. In the chick, axons from the temporal retina, the side nearer the temple, end in the front of the tectum. Nasal axons end in the back.
scenes.visual: Retina bar to tectum bar, ordered lines, neighbours highlighted, temporal to front and nasal to back
scenes.narration: The retina sends its axons to a target in the midbrain, the tectum. The map is orderly. Neighbors in the retina connect to neighbors in the tectum. In the chick, axons from the temporal retina, the side nearer the temple, end in the front of the tectum. Nasal axons end in the back.

scenes.tts: A growth cone is the moving tip of an axon. It senses only what is close, yet the map spans the whole target. The answer is a pair of opposite slopes. In the retina, the receptor Eff A is high on the temporal side and low on the nasal side. In the tectum, the ligand eff-rin A rises from front to back.
scenes.visual: Growth cone with small sensing circle, then two opposite gradient bars
scenes.caption: A growth cone is the moving tip of an axon. It senses only what is close, yet the map spans the whole target. The answer is a pair of opposite slopes. In the retina, the receptor EphA is high on the temporal side and low on the nasal side. In the tectum, the ligand ephrin-A rises from front to back.
scenes.narration: A growth cone is the moving tip of an axon. It senses only what is close, yet the map spans the whole target. The answer is a pair of opposite slopes. In the retina, the receptor EphA is high on the temporal side and low on the nasal side. In the tectum, the ligand ephrin-A rises from front to back.

scenes.tts: Temporal axons carry the most Eff A, so a little eff-rin A repels them. They stop in the front of the tectum. Nasal axons carry little Eff A and tolerate more ephrin. They travel on into the back. One simple idea is that each axon stops where its own receptor meets enough ligand.
scenes.visual: Two growth cones run along an ephrin gradient; temporal one stops early, nasal one goes far

scenes.tts: An axon might read an absolute level of Eff A, or compare itself with its neighbors. In mouse, researchers gave a random half of the retinal cells extra Eff A. If axons read absolute levels, only those cells should shift forward. Instead, the cells with extra Eff A took the front of the target, and their normal neighbors were pushed to the back. Two orderly maps filled the target together.
scenes.visual: Normal map, half the cells marked purple, absolute prediction cleared, then purple take front and blue pushed back
scenes.caption: An axon might read an absolute level of EphA, or compare itself with its neighbours. In mouse, researchers gave a random half of the retinal cells extra EphA. If axons read absolute levels, only those cells should shift forward. Instead, the cells with extra EphA took the front of the target, and their normal neighbours were pushed to the back. Two orderly maps filled the target together.
scenes.narration: An axon might read an absolute level of EphA, or compare itself with its neighbours. In mouse, researchers gave a random half of the retinal cells extra EphA. If axons read absolute levels, only those cells should shift forward. Instead, the cells with extra EphA took the front of the target, and their normal neighbours were pushed to the back. Two orderly maps filled the target together.

scenes.tts: So each axon is judged against the others. Its ending depends on its Eff A signal relative to its neighbors. Axons compete for space, and the map is the outcome. Each growth cone senses only a short distance. Yet local rules give global order, because every axon is also sensing the others.
